title: Kestrel Dispensing Standard for Prescriptions: Same Drug and Strength on Two Records
content:
Prescriptions of one patient under Kestrel Prescriptions for the same drug name and drug strength are aggregated.

## Clause 1 — Replacement

When a newer prescription for the same drug and strength is entered while an older one is in received or active status, the newer one replaces it: the older prescription is discontinued on the date the newer one's original fill is dispensed, and the two are never filled side by side. Supply on hand is counted across both records.

## Clause 2 — Earliest original fill of the replacing prescription

The original fill of a prescription that replaces another prescription for the same drug and strength is dispensed no earlier than the most recent dispensed fill of that drug and strength plus the refill-eligibility days.

- **Clock start:** the dispensing date of the most recent dispensed fill of that drug and strength, as shown on the fill ledger, whichever of the two records it was dispensed on. The fill date is day 0.
- **Refill-eligibility days:** the days supply of that most recent fill multiplied by the early refill threshold percent of the newer prescription's class and divided by 100, with any fraction of a day dropped.
- **Counting:** calendar days.
- **Comparison:** the original fill is dispensed on or after the fill date plus the refill-eligibility days; the boundary day itself qualifies.
- **Evidence:** system records only — the fill ledger's dispensing date and days supply, correlated to the records of that drug and strength.

## Clause 3 — Different strength

A different strength of the same drug is a dosage change and is not aggregated here.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

| Most recent fill of the drug and strength | Newer prescription's class threshold | Refill-eligibility days | Earliest original fill of the newer prescription |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days supply, dispensed on day 0 | 80 percent | 24 | day 24 qualifies; day 23 does not |
| 28 days supply, dispensed on day 0 | 90 percent | 25 (25.2 with the fraction dropped) | day 25 qualifies; day 24 does not |
| 90 days supply, dispensed on day 0 | 80 percent | 72 | day 72 qualifies; day 71 does not |

**Which class's threshold applies when the two records are of different classes?** The threshold of the newer prescription's class.

**Is a new 20 mg prescription aggregated with an old 10 mg prescription of the same drug?** No. A different strength is a dosage change and is not aggregated under this standard.
